title: Aspect 2: Recognizing Aspect Pairs
description: Aspect pairs follow predictable form patterns. Today: prefix-added pairs, suffix-change pairs, and a few suppletive (different-root) pairs.
descriptionRussian: Видовые пары образуются по нескольким моделям: добавление приставки, замена суффикса и супплетивные пары (разные корни).
intro: Lesson 1 was about what the two halves of a pair mean. This one is about how to spot them. Most pairs differ by a prefix stuck on the front, which makes them easy to recognize once you know to look there. A smaller group differs by a syllable in the middle instead. Two pairs are simply different words, and those you learn as vocabulary.
rules: Most A2 aspect pairs are formed by ADDING a prefix to the imperfective: про-, на-, с-, по-, при-, вы-, у-. The bare verb is imperfective; the prefixed verb is perfective.
Some pairs are formed by SUFFIX CHANGE: the imperfective contains -ва-, -ова-, -ива-, or -ыва-, and the perfective is shorter. Examples: давать / дать, покупать / купить.
A few pairs are SUPPLETIVE (totally different roots): говорить / сказать, брать / взять. These have to be memorized.
Past-tense endings (-л, -ла, -ло, -ли) are independent of aspect. Both aspects use them. The aspectual difference is in the verb stem (prefix vs no prefix; long suffix vs short).
examples: покупать (НСВ) → купить (СВ): suffix change with vowel and stem shift.

tables.title: Three Patterns of Aspect Pair Formation

rows.label: Prefix added
cells: Imperfective is bare; perfective adds a one-syllable prefix

rows.label: Suppletive
cells: Different roots; memorize as separate items

items.promptEnglish: Masha was cooking dinner all morning.
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 1: 'all morning' duration cue points to which aspect?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 1: duration phrases trigger the imperfective. Готовила is the imperfective past. The pair is готовить (НСВ) / приготовить (СВ); the perfective adds the prefix при-. Today's lesson focuses on the form pattern of pairs like this one.

items.hint: 'Уже' (already) marks completion. The pair is писать / написать; the perfective adds which prefix?
items.explanation: The imperfective писать and the perfective написать differ by the prefix на-. 'Уже' (already) is a completion cue, so the perfective написал is the right form. Most A2 pairs follow this prefix-added pattern.

items.promptEnglish: Anton did the homework and went for a walk.
items.hint: 'And went for a walk' shows the action ended before the next event. The pair is делать / сделать.
items.explanation: Sequence of completed events: did the homework, then went for a walk. The first action is finished. The perfective сделал adds the prefix с-. The imperfective делать and the perfective сделать are an A2 staple pair.

items.hint: A single utterance is one completed event. The pair is говорить / сказать. Notice the roots are different.
items.explanation: Saying one thing once is a single completed speech event: perfective. The pair говорить (imperfective) / сказать (perfective) uses two completely different roots, so memorize it as a unit. Говорила (imperfective) would describe ongoing or repeated speech, not a single utterance.

items.promptEnglish: Anton bought the book at the shop.
items.hint: Single completed transaction. The pair is покупать / купить. Which is shorter?
items.explanation: Купил is the perfective of покупать. This is a SUFFIX-CHANGE pair: the imperfective покупать is longer (with -а-); the perfective купить is shorter (with -и-). When you see a -ва- / -ова- / -ива- in the imperfective, look for a shorter perfective.

items.promptEnglish: I drank a cup of coffee and left.
items.hint: Drank the cup, then left. The pair is пить / выпить. Which prefix marks the perfective?
items.explanation: Sequence of two finished events: drank, left. Perfective выпил. The prefix вы- marks the perfective; the bare пить is imperfective. Past masculine ending -л, same as in пил and ушёл.

blanks: Я _____ суп и съел его. (I cooked the soup and ate it.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Two completed events in sequence (cooked, ate) point to the perfective. Приготовил is the perfective of готовить, formed by adding the prefix при-. The imperfective готовил would describe only the cooking process, leaving the result unclear.

errorCorrection.sentence: Вчера Антон побрал книгу в библиотеке.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Yesterday Anton took out a book at the library.
errorCorrection.explanation: The perfective partner of брать (to take) is взять, a completely different root, not a prefixed form of брать. Взял marks the single completed act of taking the book. Побрал is not a real word; it is what a learner builds by adding по- to брать. Брал is the imperfective past.

errorCorrection.sentence: Маша долго искала телефон и наконец поискала его.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha searched for her phone for a long time and finally found it.
errorCorrection.explanation: The pair искать / найти uses two different roots: the perfective 'found' is нашла, not a prefixed form of искать. Поискала is a real word but means 'searched for a while' - it does not mean the search succeeded, so 'наконец поискала' is wrong. Искала is the imperfective past.

errorCorrection.sentence: Утром я побрал зонт, потому что шёл дождь.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: In the morning I took an umbrella because it was raining.
errorCorrection.explanation: Брать and взять are a completely different-root pair: the perfective взять (past взял) is not a prefixed form of брать. Побрал is not a real word; it is invented by adding по- to the imperfective. Imperfective брал would describe a repeated or ongoing action ('used to take'), but taking the umbrella once that morning is a single completed act. Возьму is the perfective future ('I will take'), which the past context rules out.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I read the book through in an hour.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'За час' (in an hour) measures completion time, a perfective cue. The pair is читать / прочитать; the perfective adds the prefix про-. Прочитал is the right form.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Anton was writing the article all morning.
minimalPairs.explanation: 'Всё утро' is a duration cue, pointing to the imperfective. The bare писал is imperfective; the prefixed написал would mark completion, which the sentence does not claim.

reviewVocab.definition: aspectual pair (an imperfective verb together with its perfective counterpart, sharing a meaning but differing in aspect)
reviewVocab.example: Видовая пара 'читать / прочитать' выражает одно действие в двух видах.

reviewVocab.definition: formation of aspect (the way the perfective is built from the imperfective: adding a prefix, changing the suffix, or using a different root)
reviewVocab.example: Образование вида 'писать / написать' — добавление приставки на-.

reviewVocab.definition: meaning (here: the meaning difference between the two aspects, even when both translate to the same English verb)
reviewVocab.example: Значение видов — это разница между процессом и результатом.
